'''Stephanie Jutta Schwabe''' (born 1 January 1957 in [[Germany]]) is a [[Geomicrobiology|geomicrobiologist]]. She completed a [[Ph.D.]] in the [[Biogeochemistry|biogeochemical]] investigation of caves within the [[The Bahamas|Bahamian]] [[carbonate platform]]s. She is an expert [[Geology|geologic]] [[Underwater diving|diver]] mostly in Bahamian blues holes, though her experience extends to expeditions in U.S. waters. ''Diver International'' named her one of the top cave 40 divers in the world in 1997.

Schwabe earned a degree in law at the [[University of Queensland]] with a focus on [[international environmental law]] in 2003.<ref name="Geotimes2008" /> She also earned a graduate degrees at the [[College of Charleston]] in South Carolina and [[Mississippi State University]], and a [[doctorate]] from the [[University of Bristol]] in England.<ref name="Warren2011" />

Schwabe works as a professor at the [[Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, University of Manchester|Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences]] and as a scientist at the [[University of Kentucky]].<ref name="Warren2011" /><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Underwater Cave Diving in the Bahamas: Stephanie Schwabe {{!}} University of Kentucky College of Arts & Sciences |url=https://www.as.uky.edu/podcasts/underwater-cave-diving-bahamas-stephanie-schwabe |access-date=2024-03-31 |website=www.as.uky.edu}}</ref>

Schwabe is a fellow of the [[Royal Geographical Society]] of London. She was named a [[NASA]] fellow in [[exobiology]] for her discovery of a unique life system found only in the black fresh water holes in the Bahamas, and was featured in the book titled ''Women of Discovery: A Celebration of Intrepid Women Who Explored the World''.<ref name="Wings2004">{{cite web |author= |date=2009-11-19 |title=Stephanie Jutta Schwabe, 2004 Women of Discovery Courage Award |url=http://explore.wingsworldquest.org/Stephanie_Schwabe |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110815232008/explore.wingsworldquest.org/Stephanie_Schwabe |archive-date=2011-08-15 |access-date=2021-02-20 |publisher=Wings WorldQuest}}</ref><ref name=Polk2001>{{cite book |author1=Polk, Milbry |author2=Tiegreen, Mary |title=Women of Discovery: A Celebration of Intrepid Women Who Explored the World |isbn=0-609-60480-5 |publisher=Clarkson Potter Publishers |year=2001}}</ref>

In 2004, Schwabe was given the [[Women of Discovery Awards|Women of Discovery Award]] for Courage by Wings WorldQuest.<ref name=Wings2004/>

==Exploration==
Schwabe began diving in caves either in the mid-1980s<ref name="Warren2011" /> or in 1992.<ref name=Geotimes2008>{{cite web |author=Wayman, Erin |title=Stephanie Schwabe |publisher=[[Geotimes#EARTH Magazine|Geotimes]] |date=July 2008 |url=http://www.agiweb.org/geotimes/july08/article.html?id=profiles.html |access-date=2001-03-14}}</ref> Since that time, she has participated in eighteen scientific expeditions to the Bahamas, as subjects for masters and doctoral research. She has participated in a number of film expeditions. In 2000, Schwabe's discovery quest led her to the Black Hole of [[Andros, Bahamas]].<ref name="Warren2011" />

Schwabe discovered a species of [[purple sulfur bacteria]] she named ''Allocromatium palmerii'' in 2003 after her late husband and diver Rob Palmer.<ref>{{cite web |author=staff |title=Exploring the Black (and Blue) Holes of the Bahamas |url=http://www.licor.com/env/newsline/2011/03/1905/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181201045049/http://www.licor.com/env/newsline/2011/03/1905/ |archive-date=1 December 2018 |access-date=10 November 2024 |publisher=LI-COR Biosciences}}</ref><ref name=DiverNet>{{cite web |author=Schwabe, Stephanie |title=The floor on fire |publisher=Diver Magazine |url=http://www.divernet.com/other_diving_topics/cave_diving/160902/the_floor_of_fire.html |access-date=2001-03-14 |archive-date=2011-07-10 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110710134458/http://www.divernet.com/other_diving_topics/cave_diving/160902/the_floor_of_fire.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Schwabe is the founder and director of the Rob Palmer Blues Holes Foundation, a nonprofit organization.<ref name=FoundationDir>{{cite web |author=staff |title=About: Stephanie Jutta Schwabe Founder and Director of the Rob Palmer Blue Holes Foundation |url=http://www.blueholes.org/The%20Rob%20Palmer%20Blue%20Holes%20Foundation/About%20Founder.html |access-date=2001-03-14}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> The foundation is dedicated to the scientific and physical exploration of blue holes within the Bahamas and related environment. The foundation's goals are to encourage education and conservation of Bahamian caves and blue holes.<ref name=FoundationObj>{{cite web |author=staff |title=Objectives |url=http://www.blueholes.org/The%20Rob%20Palmer%20Blue%20Holes%20Foundation/Objectives.html |access-date=2001-03-14}}</ref>

Schwabe also describes the [[Third Man phenomenon]] that occurred to her while lost as she was [[solo diving]] in a cave.<ref name=NPR>{{cite news |author=Geiger, John |title=Guardian Angels Or The 'Third Man Factor'? |publisher=[[NPR]] |date=2009-09-13 |url=https://www.npr.org/templates/story/story.php?storyId=112746464 |access-date=2001-03-14 |author-link=John G. Geiger}}</ref>

Her husband, British diving pioneer Rob Palmer, died on a pleasure dive in the Red Sea in 1997.<ref name=Warren2011>{{cite news |author=Warren, Jim |date=2011-03-15 |publisher=Lexington Herald |title=UK scientist has her lab in underwater caves |url=https://www.kentucky.com/news/local/education/article44084328.html |access-date=2021-02-20}}</ref>
